correctness.rationale: All vertex/midpoint pairwise distances are explicitly derived by nearest cube endpoints. The Walsh identity block diagonalizes all coordinates; three frequency regimes and direct determinant/traces yield the displayed spectra for every d. The counted blocks sum to N, the zero-frequency compression is treated rather than merely deleting an eigenvalue, all singleton eigenvalues have negative trace and positive determinant, and d=1,2 boundaries are checked separately. Independently constructed BFS distances, exact integer block equations and obstruction witnesses support the proof for d=1..6; finite tests are not the universal argument.

originality.rationale: No covering claim was found after examining three especially plausible full texts and published scientific search records. Their closest theorems concern Laplacian/effective resistance on the same subdivision, geodesic-distance spectra of non-subdivided cube families, or subdivisions of distinct minimal cages. None implies the complete centered geodesic distance spectrum for arbitrary S(Q_d). A concealed equivalent in historical distance-spectral literature remains possible.

value.rationale: The problem uses a canonical infinite family of network subdivisions and the natural geodesic distance kernel; the exact spectral classification identifies a dimension-three transition destroying conditionally negative type despite the original Hamming metric being of negative type. The complete eigenvalue list and explicit all-dimensional positive witness reveal why subdivision changes Gaussian positivity and support future analysis of graph metric embeddings. It is not an arbitrary small computation or a numerical observation.
